elaine: opened PR to consolidate streaming + pagination snippets across py/ts/go. https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/534. goals: canonicalize resume cursor to "" (start), show per-call deadline patterns, and add a tiny knob cheat for quick ops. please review.
raj: quick glance 1: agree canonical cursor is helpful. for TS show AbortController + stop-after-N pattern. note that abort may still emit final partial event from server.
miguel: for Python prefer `async for chunk in client.responses.stream(...)` and wrap the whole call in `asyncio.wait_for(..., timeout=0.25)` to bound the call. avoids manual loop mistakes.
raj: TS snippet suggestion: ```ts
const ac = new AbortController();
const s = client.responses.stream({model: 'redwood-mini', input: q, signal: ac.signal});
let seen = 0;
for await (const p of s) { handle(p); if (++seen >= 40) ac.abort(); }
```
miguel: Python snippet: ```py
async def run(q):
  async for c in client.responses.stream(model='redwood-mini', input=q):
    handle(c)
await asyncio.wait_for(run(q), timeout=0.25)
```
elaine: Go snippet will show `context.WithTimeout` and include resume token header example so readers see both patterns. Also normalized every pagination example to use `cursor: ""` and added a one-line note: "Use "" to request the first page; server may return an opaque resume token for subsequent pages."
raj: added a compact knob line under examples: "batching -> higher throughput; per-call deadlines -> bounded latency; TTL cache -> fewer cold starts."
docs-bot: PR 534 updated: snippet smoke-tests passed and docs linter green.
elaine: merging in 15m unless any objections. thanks!
